text: The minimum biofilm eradication concentration (MBEC) of an antibiotic is typically much higher (often 10 to 1000 times) than the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) for the same bacteria grown planktonically.
explanation: True. Killing bacteria embedded in a biofilm requires far higher antibiotic concentrations than killing planktonic cells, because of matrix barriers, metabolic dormancy, and metabolic heterogeneity. This MIC/MBEC gap is a central reason biofilm infections fail treatment at doses effective against planktonic infections.
